title: The 10 Best Cordless Right Angle Drills
subtitle: Compact and heavy-duty right-angle drills for tight spaces, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A right-angle drill puts the chuck at 90 degrees so you can drill and drive between studs, inside cabinets and under sinks. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Milwaukee, RYOBI, Bosch, Makita and value brands on rating, review volume and features (a brushless motor, 300 in-lb or more of torque, a clutch and a battery in the box).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: RYOBI ONE+ HP 18V Brushless Compact 3/8" Right Angle Drill, Tool Only (PSBRA02B)
products.best_for: RYOBI owners who need to drill in tight spots.
products.verdict: A brushless RYOBI right-angle drill with 350 in-lb of torque, rated 4.7 stars, for RYOBI ONE+ owners.

specs.extras: 2x the torque of the previous model

products.name: Milwaukee M12 3/8" Cordless Right Angle Drill, Tool Only (2415-20)
products.best_for: Electricians, plumbers and cabinet installers with M12 batteries.
products.verdict: The best-selling and most-reviewed right-angle drill here: Milwaukee's compact M12 for drilling and driving between joists and inside cabinets. The listing's bullets are filler, but it's rated 4.7 stars on 1,812 reviews.

products.name: BOSCH PS11-102 12V Max 3/8" Right Angle Drill/Driver Kit with 2.0Ah Battery
products.best_for: Light drilling and driving in cabinets and tight frames.
products.verdict: A light 2.75 lb Bosch kit with a head that pivots through 5 positions from 90 to 180 degrees, for driving screws where a straight drill won't fit.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL HOLE HAWG 1/2" Right Angle Drill, Tool Only (2807-20)
products.best_for: Pros running wire and pipe through framing.
products.verdict: The tool electricians and plumbers use to bore big holes through studs and joists: Milwaukee's brushless M18 FUEL HOLE HAWG with a 1/2-inch chuck.
cons: Big and heavy for small jobs

products.name: ADOTOCAM Brushless Right Angle Drill for DEWALT 20V Battery, Tool Only (ZJ-001Z)
products.best_for: DEWALT owners who want a cheap right-angle drill.
products.verdict: A DEWALT-battery right-angle drill with a brushless motor and a claimed 400 in-lb, rated 4.8 stars on 73 reviews.

products.name: VEVOR Brushless 3/8" Cordless Right Angle Drill with Battery and Charger (DJZO5030-10)
products.verdict: A budget brushless kit with a battery, charger and 45 N-m of torque, for less than a bare Milwaukee.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL HOLE HAWG Right Angle Drill with 7/16" QUIK-LOK, Tool Only (2808-20)
products.verdict: The HOLE HAWG with a QUIK-LOK chuck for fast bit changes with self-feed and auger bits.

products.name: Alloyman 20V Brushless 3/8" Right Angle Drill with 2 x 2.0Ah Batteries (AM-HS-ZJ-DQ)
products.best_for: Budget buyers who want a complete kit.
products.verdict: A budget brushless kit with two batteries and two speeds.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 Cordless Right Angle Drill Driver, Tool Only (C18RAD-0)
products.best_for: M18 owners who drive screws in tight spaces.
products.verdict: An M18 right-angle drill/driver with an electronic clutch, so you can drive screws without stripping them. The model number (C18RAD-0) is Milwaukee's international version.

products.name: Makita XAD01Z 18V LXT 3/8" Angle Drill, Tool Only
products.best_for: Makita owners drilling in tight spots.
products.verdict: Makita's 18V angle drill with a short 2-5/8-inch head for close quarters and variable speed to 1,800 RPM.

avoid.name: ALLOYPOWER 20V Brushless Right Angle Drill with 2 x 2.0Ah Battery and Charger
avoid.flag: Same listing copy as the Alloyman kit; costs $10 more; 4.0 stars
avoid.verdict: Its bullets match the Alloyman kit word for word, it costs about $10 more, and it's rated 4.0 stars.
reasons: The motor, chuck and dual-speed bullets are the same text as the Alloyman AM-HS-ZJ-DQ listing, down to 'up to 400 in-lb', so you appear to pay more for the same tool under another name.
It's rated 4.0 stars on 18 reviews, below the Alloyman's 4.6.
If you want this design, the Alloyman listing is cheaper; if you want proven, the Milwaukee 2415-20 has 1,809 reviews.

buyers_guide.a: Drilling and driving where a normal drill won't fit: between studs and joists, inside cabinets, under sinks and in engine bays.
Compact 3/8-inch angle drills drive screws and drill small holes in tight spots. HOLE HAWG-style 1/2-inch drills bore large holes through framing for wire and pipe with self-feed and auger bits.
For screws and small holes, 115 to 150 in-lb is plenty. For bigger bits and lag screws, look for 300 in-lb or more, or a HOLE HAWG.
A right-angle attachment for your regular drill works for occasional use. A dedicated angle drill is shorter, lighter and much easier in tight spaces.
Yes for regular use: brushless motors run cooler and get more done per charge.
